newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals slip on weaker bullion.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals slip on weaker bullion.

text.p: Yen-denominated Tokyo precious metal futures ended lower across the board on Wednesday, pressured by weaker bullion prices, traders said.
Gold prices ranged from eight yen to 22 yen per gram lower. Most-active benchmark February was off 21 yen at 1,389 yen.
Traders said the falls in precious metal futures were considered to be the first major technical correction following recent strong gains.
In the bullion market, spot gold extended early losses, and was quoted at $357.85/8.35 per ounce at 0743 GMT, against $358.60/359.10 in New York on Tuesday.

"In the gold futures market, private investors were slightly on the buying side in early Tokyo trade. But overseas selling in the bullion market at around $358 per ounce forced trade house to sell gold futures, which absorbed buying," a trader said.
The trader said spot gold is likely to be sandwiched between around $353.5 and $357.5 per ounce in the near term.
In continued buoyant trade, the recent rally in platinum group metals ran out of steam. Market players were watching for further developments on the possible strike at Russian producer Norilsk.
Platinum futures ranged from 10 yen to 20 yen per gram lower, with benchmark February ending down 13 yen at 1,478 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from flat to 16 yen per gram lower. Benchmark February was down two at 571 yen.

"Private investors were taking profits. But fundamentally prices have more room to gain on lingering concerns over Russian supply fears," one trader said. Traders said no shipments of platinum group metals from Russia were expected in March and April, given the fact that Russa had not yet given Japanese traders a schedule for talks. Benchmark February silver was down 2.3 yen per 10 grams at 205.9 yen.
